final_candidates.decision_summary: N236 lies in an NST sequon on a surface loop; removing the glycan may improve receptor/F accessibility while retaining loop stability.
Adjacent to N236 in the same loop, alanine may subtly alter loop conformation to favor G-mediated entry without severe disruption.
Conservative aromatic replacement may fine-tune a hydrophobic/receptor-adjacent interface while limiting structural perturbation.

stop_reason.detail: Self-review suggests the current top-3 are the most defensible candidates given limited evidence.

history.rationale: Removes the N-linked glycosylation sequon at N236, which may reduce glycan shielding of the receptor-binding surface and improve ephrin-B2/B3 access without altering the local backbone.
N236 lies within an NST sequon in a surface loop; removing this glycan may improve receptor/F accessibility, but stability uncertainty keeps confidence moderate.
Disrupts the same N236 glycosylation sequon from the third position, likely reducing glycan occupancy while preserving the N236 side chain and local hydrogen bonding.
Adjacent to N236 in the same loop; an alanine may subtly alter loop conformation to favor G-mediated entry without severe disruption.
L114 lies near the G stalk/head transition; alanine substitution may increase stalk flexibility and lower the activation barrier for F triggering after receptor engagement.
L114 is likely buried in a hydrophobic core; alanine substitution would destabilize the glycoprotein and impair entry.

rejection.reason: L114 is likely buried in a hydrophobic core; alanine substitution would destabilize the glycoprotein and impair entry.

history.rationale: Conservative aromatic substitution in a secondary receptor-binding loop may preserve hydrophobic packing while adding a hydroxyl to form a new polar contact with ephrin-B2.
Conservative aromatic replacement may fine-tune a hydrophobic/receptor-adjacent interface while limiting structural perturbation.
Removing a negatively charged side chain near the receptor-binding interface may reduce electrostatic repulsion with acidic residues on ephrin-B2, modestly increasing binding.
D445 is adjacent to W449 and likely contributes to a charged interaction network; charge removal is probably destabilizing.

rejection.reason: D445 is adjacent to W449 and likely contributes to a charged interaction network; charge removal is probably destabilizing.

history.rationale: I502 packs near the key W503 aromatic in the C-terminal binding loop; a smaller side chain could permit loop rearrangement that improves ephrin-B2 pocket fit.
I502 packs near the receptor-binding site; alanine substitution would likely disrupt critical hydrophobic packing.

rejection.reason: I502 packs near the receptor-binding site; alanine substitution would likely disrupt critical hydrophobic packing.

history.rationale: Removes the tyrosine hydroxyl while retaining aromatic packing, potentially fine-tuning the receptor interface and slowing off-rate without large structural disruption.
Conservative removal of the phenolic hydroxyl may alter an H-bond network involved in triggering F, but the aromatic side chain is preserved.
P520 is in a terminal loop near the membrane-proximal region; substitution to leucine may alter loop dynamics and enhance coupling to F fusion activation.
Proline in a turn near the C-terminal PK motif; replacement with leucine likely disrupts backbone conformation.

rejection.reason: Proline in a turn near the C-terminal PK motif; replacement with leucine likely disrupts backbone conformation.

history.rationale: Neutralizes a charged side chain in the receptor-binding pocket while retaining hydrogen-bonding potential, possibly improving electrostatic complementarity to ephrin-B2.
E435 is adjacent to W434 in a conserved structural region; neutralizing this charge likely destabilizes local structure.

rejection.reason: E435 is adjacent to W434 in a conserved structural region; neutralizing this charge likely destabilizes local structure.

history.rationale: E431 is a known receptor-binding residue; glutamine substitution may reduce charge repulsion while partially preserving side-chain interactions, but is likely risky.
Charge neutralization near a conserved cysteine/tryptophan region is unlikely to improve entry and risks structural integrity.

rejection.reason: Charge neutralization near a conserved cysteine/tryptophan region is unlikely to improve entry and risks structural integrity.
